title: 1981 AHSME Problem 8
statement: For all positive numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z,\) the product \[ \begin{aligned} &(x+y+z)^{-1}\\ &\quad\cdot(x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1})\\ &\quad\cdot(xy+yz+zx)^{-1}\\ &\quad\cdot\big((xy)^{-1}+(yz)^{-1}+(zx)^{-1}\big) \end{aligned} \] equals

solutions.text:
We have \[ x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1}=\frac{xy+yz+zx}{xyz} \] and \[ \begin{aligned} &(xy)^{-1}+(yz)^{-1}\\ &\quad+(zx)^{-1} =\frac{x+y+z}{xyz}. \end{aligned} \] All symmetric sum factors cancel, leaving \(\frac{1}{x^2y^2z^2}=x^{-2}y^{-2}z^{-2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Rewrite each sum of reciprocals over a common denominator
The two reciprocal sums introduce factors \(xy+yz+zx\) and \(x+y+z\)
